$comment: The starting system at the galactic centre, per design-bible §1. Four race homeworlds and the capital world's trading hub. Radii are already at the 1:10 universe scale (ADR-0001) — the scale is applied once here in authored content, never at conversion time, so a body's radius means the same thing everywhere it is read. TODO(name): every name below is a placeholder; the races and factions are still unnamed.

systems.name: Origin
systems.$comment: Galaxy-space coordinates are int64 kilometres and never enter Unreal (ADR-0001). The starting system sits at the origin because every player begins here; nothing else is authored yet, so there is nothing for it to be offset from.

$bodyPositionComment: These are spaced for the radius bodies are DRAWN at -- 20 km, compiled into the client -- not for radiusKm, which is the 1:10 figure and drives nothing at runtime. A ship does 2 km/s, so 200 km is under two minutes. Every pair is at least 182 km apart, which is 142 km of clear space between two 20 km surfaces. Task 157.

bodies.name: Terra
bodies.$comment: Earth-analog. 6371 km at true scale becomes 637.1 at 1:10.
bodies.$systemPositionComment: 190 km from the Capital, about a hundred seconds of flight.
bodies.$appearanceComment: Oceanic and green where it is low, weathered grey stone up high, concrete-coloured rock: Terra is humanity's scarred cradle rather than a garden.
bodies.$terrainComment: Coastal and worn. Middling frequency: real hills and valleys, nothing jagged, because Terra is an old world that has been weathered and lived on.

bodies.name: Ares
bodies.$comment: Mars-analog: thin atmosphere, red desert, low gravity.
bodies.$systemPositionComment: 184 km from the Capital, and 183 from Grimhold: the closest pair authored.
bodies.$appearanceComment: Red oxide basins rising to pale dust, bare basalt on anything steep. The palette the terrain material was first tuned against.
bodies.$terrainComment: Rugged and broken — canyons and rift valleys carved by ancient water and tectonics, per the sheet. The frequency the terrain material was tuned against.

bodies.name: Verdance
bodies.$comment: Lush and luminous — a planet that reads as alive.
bodies.$systemPositionComment: 207 km from the Capital, the far side of the system from Ares.
bodies.$appearanceComment: Deep forest floor to lit canopy green, damp bark-dark rock. Amber bioluminescence belongs to the structures rather than the ground.
bodies.$terrainComment: Softer and lower: lush basins and rolling canopy rather than crags. Gentler relief so valleys hold together as valleys.

bodies.name: Grimhold
bodies.$comment: Dark and industrial, heavy gravity, perpetual overcast. Larger than the rest, which is where the heavy gravity comes from.
bodies.$systemPositionComment: 224 km from the Capital, and the only body well off the ecliptic.
bodies.$appearanceComment: Black slag to ash-grey, basalt throughout. Nearly monochrome on purpose: the colour on Grimhold comes from its forges, not its ground.
bodies.$terrainComment: The harshest of the five. Higher relief and the finest features: scarred highlands, slag ridges and deep excavation country, and the heavy gravity to make climbing it mean something.

bodies.name: The Capital
bodies.$comment: The shared capital world the onboarding questline ends at. Neutral ground: both factions trade here, which is why career questlines live here rather than on a homeworld.
bodies.$systemPositionComment: Unchanged, and it must stay unchanged: the client's compiled-in starting planet is at this point, and the character spawn is measured from it before any of this arrives over HTTP.
bodies.$appearanceComment: Temperate and built-over. Between Terra and Ares in tone because the Capital is where everybody meets.
bodies.$terrainComment: Deliberately the tamest. The Capital is built over, and broad gentle ground is what a city sprawls across — jagged terrain here would fight every settlement placed on it.

$appearanceRanges: Height and slope thresholds are measured per body rather than shared: each world's terrain settings put its height and steepness in a different part of 0..1, and thresholds tuned against one compress another into a corner. Measured across five patches per body — capital reaches 12 degrees at its steepest and grimhold 46, so a single slope range gave one almost no rock and the other nothing but. Re-measure if a body's terrain block changes.
$nodeComment: Deposits are placed by direction from the body centre, never by latitude and longitude — a lat-long pair has two singular points and a deposit at a pole is no less valid than one at the equator. No altitude: how high the ground is there is a question the terrain function already answers, and a second answer would be free to disagree with it.
$capitalOreComment: The Capital had three ferrite deposits until 9 October 2026: node_test_player_spawn_ferrite_a, node_capital_ferrite_a and node_capital_ferrite_b. Ferrite became Terra's alone that day (task 184), and a planet-locked material may occur on one body, so they went. --seed removes a deposit content no longer authors, together with its pool; before task 184 it never removed one, and a deposit deleted here would have gone on being served from the database.

resourceNodes.$comment: Scrap, and the reason the onboarding questline was unplayable: its first step asks for 8 scrap_alloy and nothing in the world produced any. Gathering rather than mining, and requiredLevel 1 with no tool, because this is the first thing a brand-new character does and every gate after it depends on getting through this one.
resourceNodes.$directionComment: On the face a character spawns on at the Capital, about 800 m from Borlash. A new player should not have to circumnavigate a planet to find step one, and a deposit they cannot find is indistinguishable from one that does not exist. That was once written as an intention and was false for weeks: until 24 August the whole starter cluster sat 31 km away, a quarter of the way round the planet, after task 120 put players on the ground at +Z. Kept on the Capital since scrap is common to every world (task 184); whether the Capital should keep any deposits at all is design-bible section 4's open question.

resourceNodes.$starterComment: Each homeworld's starter field (task 184): two scrap and two of that world's own ore, where a new character of that race can walk the intro questline to their first hull without leaving home (task 145). The same layout on all four worlds, measured from the outpost at the drawn 20 km radius: scrap 60 m out at bearings -35 and +35 degrees, ore 110 m at -15 and 125 m at +20, bearing 0 pointing away from the world's level-15 deposit so the two fields are on opposite sides of the building. Equal walks for every race. Scrap is inside the outpost's 100 m docking range; the ore is a short walk beyond it.

resourceNodes.$toolComment: Mining is tool-gated by design (design bible, skills table), and the onboarding questline already teaches the order: gather scrap, craft the laser, then mine. Until this field existed the gate could not be authored, so step two of the quest could be skipped entirely and mining worked bare-handed.
resourceNodes.$comment: Terra's ferrite, which was the Capital's until 9 October 2026 (task 184). Two deposits rather than the Capital's three, so Terra is provisioned exactly like the other three homeworlds.

resourceNodes.$lockedComment: One planet-locked material per homeworld (ADR-0008). Each of these four items occurs here and nowhere else, and the content validator enforces it, because 'planet-locked' silently becoming 'mostly on one planet' would dissolve hauling without anything looking broken. Higher level and slower respawn than the starter deposits: these feed the cross-faction tier, not the tutorial.
resourceNodes.$toolComment: Mining is tool-gated by design (design bible, skills table), and the onboarding questline already teaches the order: gather scrap, craft the laser, then mine. Until this field existed the gate could not be authored, so step two of the quest could be skipped entirely and mining worked bare-handed.
resourceNodes.$directionComment: A hundred and fifty metres from the outpost, the same offset Ares' deposits already had. Authored identical to the station's direction until 13 September, so the rock would have stood at the centre of the building, twelve metres inside a wall, with an eight metre gather range (task 158). SpaceMMO.Bodies.DepositsStandClearOfTheirStations measures this at the drawn radius.

resourceNodes.$skillComment: Gathered rather than mined: it is resin from a living planet, and the skill split is a small way for the four worlds to play differently rather than being reskins of each other.

$stationComment: Stations on a body are placed by direction from its centre, exactly like deposits, and carry no altitude -- the terrain function already answers how high the ground is there and a stored second answer would be free to disagree with it. A station with no body is placed by system position instead, because there is no centre for a direction to be relative to. The validator rejects both at once, since two answers to 'where is it' mean whichever the code happens to read wins.

stations.$nameComment: Borlash City since 2 October (task 168): the whole walled city is this one station -- one hangar, one book, one industry queue, its four corner docks the only berths (Joe, task 169). The key stays station_capital_hub because quest 7 docks here (plan set R11).
stations.name: Borlash
stations.$kindComment: Capital, not TradingHub. It was authored as a TradingHub until 25 August, which meant StationKind.Capital was configured in DefaultGame.ini and authored on nothing -- the capital drew the same 25 m cube as every outpost, and EveryAuthoredKindHasALook could not catch it because it checks that authored kinds have a look, not that configured kinds are authored.
stations.$directionComment: About 500 m from where a character spawns, near the Capital's scrap: close enough to see and walk to, far enough that a 40 m building is not standing on top of the arrival point. Written when every new character began here. Once task 145 lands, a new character begins at their own homeworld's outpost, where task 184 put the starter deposits, and arrives here at the end of the questline.
stations.$dockingRangeComment: The whole platform, 420 m, since 2 October (task 169). It was a hundred metres because how far you can dock from is how far a ship can vanish from (task 153) -- but a ship at Borlash now docks only on one of its four landing pads, whatever this says, so this governs a person on foot alone, and a pilot set down at a corner dock 370 m from the centre must still be docked when they arrive. It still does not reach the spawn point, 500 m out, which is what the hundred metres was first protecting.
stations.$padComment: The ground Borlash stands on, levelled in the height function itself so a dedicated server stands players on the same ground the client draws (task 168). Flat for 420 m: the city's platform reaches 400 m at its corner docks (Borlash_manifest.json, pad_required), and SpaceMMO.Terrain.AuthoredPadsFitTheirCities checks the two against each other. At 172 m, just above the highest natural ground inside it (171.2 m, surveyed with the terrain function) so the city stands on a slight rise and no hillock pokes through its paving. Eases back into the land over 150 m.

stations.name: Terra Outpost
stations.$directionComment: Near that world's own locked deposit, so the material and the place to sell it are not on opposite hemispheres.

stations.$comment: The first station that orbits nothing, and the reason the deep-space branch is real rather than theoretical. A Spaceport rather than a market: this is where refitting and industry belong once station interiors exist, and keeping it distinct from the trading hubs from the start means the two never quietly become the same thing.
stations.name: Deepdock
stations.$positionComment: Between the capital and Terra, off the plane, so reaching it is a decision rather than something that happens on the way to somewhere else.
stations.$dockingRangeComment: Five hundred metres rather than the hundred the planetary stations use. Finding a 25 m cube in empty space is a different task from flying up to a building standing on a hillside you can see from the air, and until something draws where Deepdock is, the wider ring is what makes it reachable at all.
